title: All tau_k-maximal graphs have the same size

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
A graph is τk-maximal if none of its subgraphs has k+1 edge-disjoint spanning trees, but adding any missing edge creates such a subgraph. Wang and Tian conjectured that every τk-maximal graph on n ≥ 2k+2 vertices has exactly (k+1)(n-1)-1 edges. We prove this conjecture: a graph is τk-maximal if and only if it has (k+1)(n-1)-1 edges and every set X of at least two vertices spans at most (k+1)(|X|-1)-1 of them. For k = 1 these are exactly the Laman graphs.

The archive contains the paper (PDF, LaTeX sources with the figure as PNG, arXiv tarball) and independent checks in C, C++, Bash, Python, Julia and Lean 4. The C program checks every labelled graph on up to seven vertices for k = 1, 2, 3, deciding the existence of edge-disjoint spanning trees directly; for k = 1 its isomorphism-class counts 1, 3, 13, 70 match the counts of minimally rigid graphs in OEIS A227117. A Lean 4 proof with Mathlib proves, for every n and k and with only the standard axioms, every step after the Nash-Williams–Tutte theorem: the exchange lemma, the example, and the characterization of maximal sparse edge sets.
